title: Classic Sea Bass Crudo with Lemon, Chilli and Olive Oil
summary: Glossy slices of raw sea bass seasoned with lemon, flaky salt and pepper, then finished with chilli, lemon zest, olive oil and parsley.

ingredients.note: zest finely grated, plus 1 tbsp juice

ingredients.item: red chilli, sliced into thin rings

steps.title: Chill the plates
steps.text: Put the plates in the fridge for 15 min, and leave the fish there too until you are ready to cut. Cold fish slices more neatly and tastes cleaner.

steps.title: Cut thin slices
steps.text: Slice the fillet against the grain into 5 mm pieces, drawing the knife through in one long motion. Fan them loosely over the plates.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Just before serving, spoon the lemon juice over the fish, then add the flaky salt and the pepper. Salt goes on last so the crystals stay crunchy rather than dissolving.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Scatter on the chilli rings and lemon zest, drizzle each plate with a teaspoon of oil and add the parsley leaves. Serve at once, while the fish still looks glossy.

tips: RAW NOTE: the fish is eaten raw. Buy sushi- or sashimi-grade fish from a fishmonger you trust that has been frozen first (-20 °C for 7 days or -35 °C for 15 hours), keep it in the fridge until the last minute and eat it the same day. Pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should skip it.
A common mistake is dressing the fish ahead of time; the lemon starts to cure it and dulls the texture.
Use your best, freshest olive oil, since it is a main flavour here.
Bream or scallops work in the same way.
storage: Crudo cannot be stored; serve it straight away and discard leftovers. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
